3(a).stem_md:
Given the cost function of a firm
$\text{Cost} = 300x - 10x^2 + (1/3)x^3$,
**Calculate:**
(i) Output at which Marginal Cost is minimum.
(ii) Output at which Average Cost is minimum.
(iii) Output at which Marginal Cost = Average Cost.
3(a).answer_md:
(i) $\text{Cost} = 300x - 10x^2 + \frac{1}{3}x^3$

Marginal Cost $= \frac{dc}{dx} = 300 - 20x + x^2$ (say, y)
In order that MC is minimum first derivative must be equal to zero and 2nd derivative must be positive.
Therefore $\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x - 20 \Rightarrow 2x = 20$
$x = 10$
$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 2$, which is positive. It is minimum at $x = 10$.

(ii) Average Cost $= 300 - 10x + \frac{1}{3}x^2$ (y say)

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{dy}{dx} &= -10 + \frac{2}{3}x = 0 \\
&\Rightarrow x = 30/2 = 15 \\
\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} &= \frac{2}{3} > 0,
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, Average Cost is minimum of output at $x = 15$

(iii) Output at which Marginal Cost = Average Cost

$$
\begin{aligned}
300 - 20x + x^2 &= 300 - 10x + \frac{1}{3}x^2 \\
-20x + 10x + x^2 - \frac{1}{3}x^2 &= 0 \\
-10x + \frac{2}{3}x^2 &= 0 \\
\frac{-30x + 2x^2}{3} &= 0 \\
2x^2 - 30x &= 0 \\
2x(x - 15) &= 0 \\
x - 15 &= 0
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x = 15$

7(a).answer_md:
Let the value of Sandy Co. and Vindi Co. be represented as $PV_S$ and $PV_V$ and the value of the combined firm $PV_{SV}$.
(i) Gain from the Merger:
Gain from the merger = reduction of costs due to the merger.
Sandy Co estimates that by combining the two companies, it will reduce marketing and administrative costs by ₹ 50000 per year perpetually.
Cost of capital = 10%
Hence, $\text{PV of gain} = \text{₹ }50000/10\% = \text{₹ }500000$
(ii) Cost of the Cash Offer:
$= \text{₹ }1400000 - \text{₹ }1000000 = \text{₹ }400000$
(iii) Cost of the Stock Alternative:
When the sellers receive N shares worth $PV_{SV}$, the cost is given as
$\text{Cost} = N \times PV_{SV} - PV_V$
Here, 50% of the combined value of the firm is paid as stock.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Combined Firm Value} &= \text{Gain} + (PV_S + PV_V) \\
&= \text{₹ }500000 + \text{₹ }(2000000 + 1000000) = \text{₹ }3500000.
\end{aligned}
$$

Hence $\text{Value of Stock offered} = 0.50 \times \text{₹ }3500000 = \text{₹ }1750000$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Hence, cost of the stock alternative} &= \text{₹ }1750000 - \text{₹ }1000000. \\
&= \text{₹ }750000.
\end{aligned}
$$
